description: Architecture claims audit with precise status classification

status_definitions.PROVEN: Mathematically derived or verified by comprehensive testing with no known counterexamples
status_definitions.EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED: Verified by measurement under specific conditions; may not hold in all configurations
status_definitions.CONDITIONALLY TRUE: True under specific conditions (e.g., specific hyperparameters, scales, or configurations)
status_definitions.PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED: Code exists but is not fully wired into the model or has known gaps
status_definitions.FALSE: Claimed but not true (either was never true, or regressed)

claims.claim: SSM uses proper ZOH discretization for both A and B
claims.implementation: discretize_zoh() in ssm_scan.py computes A_bar=exp(dt*A) and B_bar=((exp(dt*A)-1)/A)*B with Taylor fallback for small |dt*A|.
claims.test: tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_ssm_zoh_discretization_stable; Phase 9 numerical equivalence (8 configs, fp32+bf16)
claims.evidence: All 8 numerical equivalence configs pass tolerance (fp32 <1e-4, bf16 <1e-2). Gradient equivalence verified for A_bar and B_bar (err < 1e-6).
claims.limitations: Only diagonal A is supported. Dense A would require matrix exponential.

claims.claim: SSM scan has O(L) sequential complexity
claims.implementation: sequential_scan: Python loop over T, vectorized over B and N. T iterations.
claims.test: Phase 9.4 complexity analysis with empirical timing at T=64..2048
claims.evidence: Theoretical: O(T*N) work, O(T) depth, O(T*N) memory. Empirical: linear scaling confirmed.
claims.limitations: Sequential is the slowest of the three scans on CPU due to Python loop overhead.

claims.claim: Parallel scan has O(L log L) work and O(log L) depth (Hillis-Steele)
claims.implementation: parallel_scan: log2(T) iterations, each touches all T elements. Pure PyTorch, no Python loop over T.
claims.test: Phase 9.4 complexity analysis
claims.evidence: Theoretical: O(T*log(T)*N) work, O(log T) depth, O(T*log(T)*N) memory. Empirical: faster than chunked on CPU at T=2048 (1.5ms vs 12ms) because no Python loop.
claims.limitations: On GPU, the O(T log T) work would make it slower than chunked for very large T. Memory is O(T log T) due to per-step clones for autograd safety.

claims.claim: Chunked scan has O(L) work with O(L/chunk + chunk) depth
claims.implementation: chunked_scan: T/chunk_size Python iterations, each runs sequential_scan on a chunk.
claims.test: Phase 9.4
claims.evidence: Theoretical: O(T*N) work, O(T/chunk + chunk) depth, O(chunk*N) memory. Empirical: 12ms at T=2048, chunk=256.
claims.limitations: Python loop over T/chunk_size limits GPU parallelism. Optimal chunk_size depends on hardware.

claims.claim: SSM is numerically stable at long sequences (16K+)
claims.implementation: chunked_scan with LayerNorm on states (ln_state in SSMPathway).
claims.test: Phase 9.3: T=1024, 4096, 16384 all produce finite states and gradients.
claims.evidence: T=16384: state_max=0.63, grad_max=5.89, all finite. No NaN/Inf.
claims.limitations: Not tested at 32K due to memory constraints on this hardware. Stability depends on A_bar being in (0,1) — unstable A would cause divergence.

claims.claim: Depth routing genuinely skips computation (gather-scatter, not compute-then-mask)
claims.implementation: model.py forward: at inference, if n_active < B*T, calls block.forward_with_depth() which gathers active tokens, runs block on subset, scatters back.
claims.test: Phase 5.1: half_active mask reduces FLOPs by 27.8%, none_active by 55.5%. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_depth_gather_scatter_at_inference.
claims.evidence: OpCounter measured: all_active=8.5M FLOPs, half_active=6.1M FLOPs (27.8% reduction), none_active=3.8M FLOPs (55.5% reduction).
claims.limitations: At TRAINING, still uses STE mask blend (compute-then-mask) for differentiability. Genuine sparsity only at inference. The 27.8% reduction (vs theoretical 33%) is because embeddings/MoE/lm_head are always-on.

claims.claim: Width routing genuinely changes matmul dimensions
claims.implementation: SlicedFFN in sliced_ffn.py: fc1 maps H->W, fc2 maps W->H, where W is the selected width. Only the selected W executes.
claims.test: Phase 5.2: SlicedFFN width=16:32:64 gives FLOPs 32768:65536:131072 = 0.25:0.50:1.00. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_adaptive_ffn_sliced_width (in test_phase2_sparsity.py).
claims.evidence: Linear hook shapes confirm fc1 output dim = selected width. Analytical FLOPs scale linearly with width.
claims.limitations: SlicedFFN is NOT wired into HASSBlock — HASSBlock still uses AdaptiveFFN which computes base + all adapters and blends. Phase 15 recommendation: replace AdaptiveFFN with SlicedFFN.

claims.claim: Pathway routing genuinely skips unselected pathways (top-k sparse dispatch)
claims.implementation: sparse_pathway_dispatch in sparse_dispatch.py: for each pathway, finds tokens that selected it, only calls forward on those tokens. Pathways with no selected tokens are NOT called.
claims.test: Phase 5.3: K=1 -> only 1 pathway called, K=2 -> 2 pathways, K=3 -> all 3. Adversarial: all tokens to SSM -> only SSM called. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_pathway_top_k_1_skips_unselected.
claims.evidence: Pathway call counter: K=1 with all tokens to SSM -> {local:0, low_rank:0, ssm:1}. Confirmed 0 calls to unselected pathways.
claims.limitations: STE is used at training for differentiability. The forward uses hard top-k mask, backward sees soft probs.

claims.claim: MoE top-k genuinely executes only K experts per token
claims.implementation: ShardedExpertFabric.forward: loops over top_k slots, groups tokens by expert id within each slot. Experts that no token selects are NOT loaded/called.
claims.test: Phase 5.4: K=1 -> 1 expert called, others get zero gradient. K=2 -> 2 experts, K=3 -> 3 experts. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_moe_unselected_experts_not_called (in test_phase2_sparsity.py).
claims.evidence: Expert call counts and gradient norms verify: called experts have non-zero grad, uncalled experts have exactly zero grad.
claims.limitations: Capacity constraint can force some tokens to lower-priority experts (capacity_factor=1.25 default).

claims.claim: Genuine sparse execution achieves measurable FLOPs reduction vs dense
claims.implementation: Combined effect of SPARSE-1/2/3/4.
claims.test: Phase 13: Baseline D (genuine sparse) vs Baseline A (dense).
claims.evidence: D uses 358M FLOPs/forward vs A 603M (40.6% reduction). D trains successfully (loss 3.47 -> 0.85).
claims.limitations: At tiny scale (H=32), D is SLOWER than A in wall-clock (14.3ms vs 13.9ms) due to Python dispatch overhead. On GPU at large scale, sparse would win.

claims.claim: Path diversity loss prevents pathway collapse
claims.implementation: path_diversity_loss = -entropy(path_probs) in routing.py. Default weight 0.1 (raised from 0.02 in Phase 6).
claims.test: Phase 6: tested 4 regimes (no/weak/current/strong balancing).
claims.evidence: no_balancing: collapse to 1 pathway. weak (0.002): collapse. current (0.02): collapse. strong (0.2): partial diversity (2/3 pathways). After bumping default to 0.1, comparative test confirms strong div >= no div.
claims.limitations: Even at 0.2, only 2/3 pathways active (not full diversity). The loss is necessary but not sufficient. Width router also collapses (always picks largest) — no width diversity loss exists.

claims.claim: Expert load balancing prevents expert collapse
claims.implementation: Switch Transformer formula: L_lb = E * sum(f_e * p_e) in routing.py + L2 loss in model.py. (Phase 15 noted these double-count.)
claims.test: Phase 6: all 4 regimes had 0 dead experts, gini <= 0.057.
claims.evidence: Expert utilization is healthy across all regimes. 4/4 experts called with roughly uniform distribution.
claims.limitations: Two load-balance losses double-count. Phase 15 recommends unifying.

claims.claim: Depth routing does not collapse
claims.implementation: depth_router with min_depth=1 enforcement in _route_depth.
claims.test: Phase 4: avg_depth=3.00/3 after 200 training steps. Phase 6: all regimes avg_depth ~3.0.
claims.evidence: No depth collapse observed in any experiment.
claims.limitations: min_depth=1 forces layer 0 active, which prevents full depth collapse but also prevents maximum sparsity.

claims.claim: ComputeController allocates compute based on global budget
claims.implementation: compute_controller.py takes compute_budget in [0,1] and modulates depth/width/pathway/expert routing.
claims.test: Phase 7: measured at budgets [0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00].
claims.evidence: FLOPs monotonically increase with budget: 0.10->1.7M, 1.00->6.9M. avg_depth scales: 0.12 -> 2.34.
claims.limitations: 1) ComputeController is NOT wired into zeroModel — model uses AdaptiveRouter directly. Phase 7 tested it as a drop-in replacement. 2) Width bias had wrong sign (FIXED in Phase 7). 3) Cost model treats all ops as equal — embeddings/lm_head are always-on regardless of budget.

claims.claim: Compute budget controls actual compute (not just metadata)
claims.implementation: ComputeController.actual_compute field + OpCounter measurement.
claims.test: Phase 7: predicted_compute and actual_flops both monotonically increase with budget.
claims.evidence: Predicted and actual correlate. 4x FLOPs range across budgets.
claims.limitations: FLOPs ratio (0.244) does not match budget ratio (0.10) because always-on components dominate at low budgets.

claims.claim: Disk-sharded MoE survives save -> restart -> reload
claims.implementation: ExpertDiskManager saves/loads expert state_dicts to .pt files. Manifest tracks which experts exist (int keys converted to strings for JSON).
claims.test: Phase 10 steps 1-7: create, save, destroy, reload, verify metadata, verify weights. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_moe_restart_preserves_weights.
claims.evidence: 4/4 experts weights match exactly after restart. Manifest loads correctly.
claims.limitations: The int-key/string-key JSON bug was fixed in v0.3. expert_exists() correctly checks str(eid) in manifest.

claims.claim: LRU cache evicts least-recently-used experts
claims.implementation: LRUExpertCache uses OrderedDict, moves to end on access, evicts from front.
claims.test: Phase 10 step 10: loaded 4 experts with capacity 3, expert 0 evicted.
claims.evidence: After loading 0,1,2,3 with cap=3: cache=[1,2,3], 1 eviction. Correct LRU order.
claims.limitations: Cache is a plain Python class (not nn.Module) — Phase 10 found and fixed that .eval() did not propagate. Now overridden in ShardedExpertFabric.train().

claims.claim: Train/eval mode propagates to cached experts
claims.implementation: ShardedExpertFabric.train(mode) override propagates to all cached experts + dummy expert.
claims.test: Phase 10 step 13. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_moe_eval_mode_propagates_to_cached_experts.
claims.evidence: After fix: train() sets all cached experts to training mode, eval() sets all to eval mode.
claims.limitations: This was a BUG in v0.3 (LRUExpertCache not nn.Module). Fixed in Phase 10.

claims.claim: Architecture can train (loss decreases, gradients finite)
claims.implementation: Full differentiable forward pass with STE for routing decisions.
claims.test: Phase 4: 200 steps, loss 3.47 -> 0.006. tests/test_phase4_v04.py::test_tiny_training_loss_decreases.
claims.evidence: 99.8% loss reduction, 98.3% accuracy, all outputs finite, gradients reach all expected subsystems.
claims.limitations: CoT is frozen by design (pre-training). Pathway collapse means local + low_rank pathways get zero gradient.

claims.claim: ComputeController is part of the model architecture
claims.implementation: compute_controller.py exists but is NOT imported by zeroModel. The model uses AdaptiveRouter.
claims.test: Phase 7 needed to patch the router to test ComputeController.
claims.evidence: grep shows no import of ComputeController in zero/model.py or zmoe.py.
claims.limitations: Should either wire it in (replacing AdaptiveRouter) or remove it. Phase 15 recommendation.

claims.claim: Adaptive halting is part of the model architecture
claims.implementation: adaptive_halting.py exists but is NOT imported by zeroModel.
claims.test: grep shows no usage.
claims.evidence: Dead code.
claims.limitations: Remove or wire in.

claims.claim: SlicedFFN provides model-level width sparsity
claims.implementation: sliced_ffn.py exists and is tested, but HASSBlock uses AdaptiveFFN (compute-then-blend) instead.
claims.test: Phase 5.2 tested SlicedFFN standalone. Phase 15 noted it is not used by HASSBlock.
claims.evidence: SlicedFFN works correctly in isolation but is not wired into the model.
claims.limitations: Phase 15 recommendation: replace AdaptiveFFN with SlicedFFN in HASSBlock.

claims.claim: CoT (Chain-of-Thought) contributes to model training
claims.implementation: InternalLatentCoT is frozen (requires_grad=False) for pre-training. cot_vector_seq is zeros.
claims.test: Phase 4: CoT parameters have zero gradient (frozen).
claims.evidence: 46 leaf params have zero grad, all in low_rank pathway (due to pathway collapse) — CoT is intentionally frozen.
claims.limitations: This is BY DESIGN — CoT is for fine-tuning phase. model.enable_cot() unfreezes it. Document this clearly.
